comments.body:
CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S OWN REMEDIATION — traced the full path, and fixing the branch this ticket
names would NOT stop the duplicate. Recording before planning, because AC #2 as written ("the chosen
mitigation is applied to the keyless-pending branch") would certify a fix that still ships duplicates.

THERE ARE TWO INDEX-DEPENDENT SITES, AND THIS TICKET NAMES ONLY THE FIRST.

  1. `binding_store.recover_pending`, keyless branch (binding_store.py:521-531) — searches, and on a
     miss UNBINDS. This is the site the ticket describes.
  2. `dispatch_one.create_one`'s JQL dedup (dispatch_one.py:237-238) —
     `hits = client.search_issues(f'labels = "rebar-id:{local_id}"')`, and on a miss it CREATES.

Site 2 is the one that actually writes the second issue. Site 1 only removes the record that might
have prevented reaching site 2.

THE CHAIN, VERIFIED IN SOURCE
  a. crash during create -> keyless-pending entry (`jira_key: None`).
  b. next pass: `recover_pending` searches, misses because the issue is not yet indexed, UNBINDS.
  c. `outbound_differ.py:528-531` gates the create on `binding_store.get_jira_key(local_id) is None`.
  d. `create_one` dedup-searches, misses for the same index-lag reason, and CREATES A DUPLICATE.

WHY FIXING ONLY SITE 1 IS INSUFFICIENT — the part I got wrong on the first read. Suppose (b) is
changed to leave the entry PENDING instead of unbinding. `get_jira_key` returns `entry.get("jira_key")`
(binding_store.py:258-262), which is `None` for a keyless-pending entry. So step (c) STILL sees None,
still emits a create, and step (d) still misses. The duplicate happens anyway. The pending entry is
invisible to the only gate that decides whether to create.

Note `is_pending()` already exists at binding_store.py:270 and the differ does not consult it. The
information needed to suppress the create is present and unused.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FIX. The duplicate-preventing change must be at the CREATE GATE: while a
keyless-pending binding for this local_id is younger than an index-lag grace window, the create must be
DEFERRED, not issued. Leaving the binding pending (site 1) is still necessary — otherwise there is no
record to defer against — but it is the enabling half, not the fix.

The plan is being rewritten accordingly, and the ACs will require a test that drives the WHOLE path
(crash -> recover -> differ -> create) under a lagging-index client and asserts EXACTLY ONE issue is
created. A test that only asserts "recover_pending did not unbind" would pass while the duplicate is
still written — which is precisely the trap this correction exists to close.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
REGRESSION FOUND IN THIS TICKET'S OWN CHANGE, AND FIXED — new patchset on Gerrit 1130.

WHAT BROKE: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_create_binding.py::
test_create_one_populates_binding_store` FAILED with `assert None is not None`.

HOW I FOUND IT: a full `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` sweep run locally while waiting on CI —
1 failed, 817 passed. It was NOT caught earlier because the change's own held-out module
(`test_index_lag_duplicate_heldout.py`) passes, and the three in-flight Gerrit changes had been
sitting in a saturated Actions queue for over two hours without reporting Verified.

MECHANISM, traced rather than guessed. `create_one`'s new index-lag gate (dispatch_one.py:249-254)
reads `getattr(binding_store, "is_keyless_pending_within_grace", None)` and defers the create when
it returns truthy. That test's double is a bare `MagicMock()`, which answers EVERY member with a
truthy Mock — so the gate fired for a ticket that has no pending binding at all, the create was
deferred, and `create_one` returned None.

I CONFIRMED IT WAS MINE RATHER THAN ASSUMING: reverted ONLY `dispatch_one.py` to HEAD~1 and re-ran —
still red, which ruled out my later 7c26 commit. Then `git log -S is_keyless_pending_within_grace`
named commit 06b8702b1, this ticket's own change, as the introducer.

THE FIX: the test double now answers `is_keyless_pending_within_grace -> False`, which is what a
REAL store returns for a ticket with no pending binding. This is a test-double fidelity fix, not an
oracle weakened to fit: the test's intent ("create_one must call bind_confirm after a successful
create") is untouched and still asserted, and `bind_confirm.assert_called_once_with(...)` still
runs. Without it the double stands for a store state that cannot occur. The reason is recorded in a
comment at the mock so the next reader does not delete it as noise.

SCOPE CHECKED: this is the ONLY bare-MagicMock binding store in the test tree (grepped), so no
sibling sites are affected. Re-ran with the fix: 16 passed in the two directly-affected modules,
then 581 passed across mutate/, diffing/, binding_walk and all three held-out modules in this stack.

HOW IT LANDED IN THIS CHANGE RATHER THAN A LATER ONE: the fix belongs in the commit that introduced
the gate, or change 1130 goes green only when a LATER change happens to be applied — and Gerrit
verifies each change independently, so 1130 alone would still have earned Verified -1. The stack was
rebuilt non-interactively (amend 21fc, cherry-pick 387d and 7c26 back on top) with all three
Change-Ids preserved, so this updated the existing changes rather than forking duplicates. The
LLM-Review +1 on 1130 was correctly invalidated by the new code and needs a fresh round; 1131 and
1136 were trivial rebases and kept their votes.

LESSON, since this epic keeps recording them: a bare `MagicMock` is not a neutral stand-in for a
collaborator — every new `getattr`-guarded capability check silently changes what it answers, and
the failure surfaces as an unrelated-looking `None`. When adding a gate that consults an OPTIONAL
store member, grep the test tree for bare mocks of that collaborator in the same change.

comments.body:
REGRESSION IN THIS CHANGE, FOUND VIA CI AND FIXED — three failing tests, two distinct causes.

Gerrit 1130 patchset 6 (run 30681124591) went Verified -1 with EXACTLY three failures, IDENTICAL on
all four cells (ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and macos py3.13) — deterministic, not a flake, and no other
test failed anywhere in the matrix:

  1. test_write_ahead_recovery.py::test_keyless_pending_miss_unbinds — assert 0 == 1
  2. test_write_ahead_recovery.py::test_write_ahead_orders_pending_before_create_and_key_before_label
     — ValueError: 'bind_pending' is not in list
  3. test_write_ahead_recovery.py::test_bind_pending_persist_failure_skips_create
     — Failed: DID NOT RAISE BindingPersistError

CLASS A (failure 1) — THE TEST PINNED THE BUG. Its docstring read "A keyless-pending record whose
label search misses is unbound (create never landed)" and it asserted `recovered == 1` after a
SINGLE negative search. That is precisely the defect 21fc exists to remove: the keyless-pending state
is entered exactly when we crashed during create_issue, and one empty search is what a LIVE but
unindexed issue looks like. This is the SIBLING of test_recover_pending_not_found_in_jira
(state/test_binding_store.py), which the previous session already found and inverted — it did not
sweep for the second copy. Repaired the same way and for the same stated reason: the intent (a truly
absent issue must not strand its ticket) is preserved by ageing the entry past the grace window and
repeating the misses, and the "one miss must NOT unbind" guard is now asserted here explicitly.
The inverted test has teeth by construction — it asserts == 0 on the first miss where the old test
asserted == 1, so it cannot pass against pre-fix code.
On an error I made and corrected: I first copied the sibling's `counts[-1] == 1`, which is WRONG
here, because this test makes one miss BEFORE the loop, so the unbind lands on the 3rd overall miss
and the sequence is [0, 1, 0]. Corrected to `sum(counts) == 1` — exactly one resolution across the
sequence — which asserts the real property without pinning which call it falls on.

CLASS B (failures 2 and 3) — THE BARE-MagicMock TRAP, SECOND OCCURRENCE. Both tests build
`store = MagicMock()`. A bare MagicMock answers EVERY member with a truthy Mock, including the new
`is_keyless_pending_within_grace` gate create_one consults — so the create was DEFERRED for a ticket
with no pending binding at all. That is why `order` was empty ('bind_pending' is not in list) and why
no persist was attempted (DID NOT RAISE). Fixed by having the double answer False, which is what a
real store returns — the same idiom already used at mutate/test_outbound_create_binding.py:148.
HANDOFF #7 recorded this exact lesson after hitting it in test_create_one_populates_binding_store;
the sweep it prescribed was not completed, and these two sites are what it would have caught.

SWEEP NOW COMPLETE — the part the last pass missed. Searched the whole test tree for files that call
create_one AND construct a bare MagicMock/Mock store:
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_write_ahead_recovery.py            -> 2 sites, both FIXED here
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_create_binding.py  -> 1 site, already fixed
No other file matches, so the bare-mock exposure from this change is now closed.

VERIFICATION: 41 passed across test_write_ahead_recovery.py, state/test_binding_store.py,
test_index_lag_duplicate_heldout.py and mutate/test_outbound_create_binding.py. The fix went into
21fc's OWN commit (Change-Id I2b9e0aa7a41c6a7184f355996bdb3bbe76bc421f preserved), because Gerrit
verifies each change independently and 1130 alone would otherwise stay red.

SEPARATELY — THE "CI STALL" WAS NOT INFRA, AND THAT DIAGNOSIS COST HOURS. HANDOFF #7 recorded the
four runs as a fleet stall and posted `recheck`; the recheck just restarted the same hang. Evidence:
every non-pytest job passed, while all four pytest jobs reached 99% and emitted NOTHING for 33
minutes before a bot-side budget killed them at ~45 min (healthy is ~8 min ubuntu / ~13 min macos).
Reproduced locally: same 99% stall, and a faulthandler dump caught a thread blocked in the DC
transport's `_with_connection_retry` -> the lazy `from jira.exceptions import JIRAError`. The
decisive evidence is a controlled comparison rather than the dump: change 1129 patchset 3 HUNG on the
old base, and patchset 4 — same diff, rebased onto newer main — PASSED in 15 minutes. Only the base
differed. Current main carries 77e1 ("bound remaining network git calls"); this stack predated it.
Rebasing removed the hang and turned the runs into honest failures, which is how the three defects
above became visible at all.

compiled_state.description:
# DC index lag makes a crashed create produce a DUPLICATE Jira issue

## Context / Problem

This is the only known defect where rebar writes WRONG DATA into Jira. Every other DC gap found so far
causes rebar to read incomplete data or fail loudly; this one silently creates a SECOND Jira issue for
the same local ticket — the exact outcome the write-ahead binding protocol exists to prevent.

**Jira DC's Lucene index is eventually consistent.** Nodes poll for index changes roughly once per
second and replication can fall arbitrarily behind; Atlassian's KB and JRASERVER-70423 document a
real-world lag of 2,991 seconds (~50 minutes). A JQL search cannot see an issue that is not yet
indexed. Sound on Cloud, unsound on DC.

**There are TWO index-dependent sites, and an earlier draft of this ticket named only the first.**
That matters, because fixing only the named one leaves the duplicate fully intact:

1. `binding_store.recover_pending`, keyless branch (`binding_store.py:521-531`) — searches for the
   `rebar-id:{local_id}` label and, on a miss, UNBINDS ("the create never reached Jira").
2. `dispatch_one.create_one`'s dedup (`dispatch_one.py:237-238`) —
   `hits = client.search_issues(f'labels = "rebar-id:{local_id}"')`, and on a miss it CREATES.

Site 2 writes the duplicate. Site 1 only removes the record that might have prevented reaching it.

**The chain, verified in source:**

    a. crash during create               -> keyless-pending entry (jira_key: None)
    b. next pass: recover_pending searches, misses (unindexed), UNBINDS
    c. outbound_differ.py:528-531 gates the create on get_jira_key(local_id) is None
    d. create_one dedup-searches, misses (unindexed), CREATES A DUPLICATE

**Why fixing site 1 alone is insufficient.** Suppose (b) leaves the entry PENDING instead of
unbinding. `get_jira_key` returns `entry.get("jira_key")` (`binding_store.py:258-262`), which is
`None` for a keyless-pending entry — so (c) still emits a create and (d) still misses. The duplicate
happens anyway. The pending entry is invisible to the only gate that decides whether to create.
`is_pending()` already exists (`binding_store.py:270`) and the differ does not consult it.

The authors already engineered this hazard away where a key was known: the KEYED-pending branch's
docstring records "NO Jira search — deterministic, so a hard crash in the create->label window yields
NO duplicate." The keyless branch falls back to search precisely because no key exists.

## Approach

**Suppress the CREATE while a keyless-pending binding is inside an index-lag grace window, and stop
unbinding on a single negative search.** Both halves are required and they do different jobs: the
create gate is what prevents the duplicate; leaving the binding pending is what gives the gate
something to see.

1. **Record the evidence on the pending entry.** `recover_pending`'s keyless branch, on a negative
   search, increments a `search_miss_count` and leaves the entry PENDING rather than unbinding. The
   entry already carries `created_at` (`bind_pending`, `binding_store.py:289-297`), so its age is
   available without a schema change beyond the counter.
2. **Unbind only on corroborated absence.** Unbind when BOTH `search_miss_count >= 3` AND the entry is
   older than an index-lag grace period (default 3600s, chosen to exceed the ~2,991s lag documented in
   JRASERVER-70423). Until then the entry stays pending and the next pass retries. This converts a
   silent duplicate into a delayed-but-correct answer.
3. **Gate the create on pendingness, not just on the absent key.** The create branch is reached
   when `get_jira_key(local_id) is None`, which is ALSO true of a keyless-pending entry. The gate
   must additionally defer (not drop) the create when a keyless-pending binding for that local_id
   is younger than the grace period. This is the change that actually prevents the second issue.
   **The gate lives in `dispatch_one.create_one`, NOT in `outbound_differ`.** Two reasons, and
   the second is binding: (a) guarding at the WRITE rather than at plan time protects the actual
   create and reuses the deferred-create semantics `create_one` already has, so the mutation is
   deferred rather than dropped; (b) `outbound_differ.py` sits at EXACTLY the locked 800-LOC
   module-size cap, so nothing can be added to it.
4. `recover_pending` returns the count of RESOLVED bindings; an entry left pending is NOT resolved and
   must not be counted, or the caller reads "recovered" as "settled".

**Applied to BOTH vendors, not branched on DC.** Cloud's index is eventually consistent too — it is
merely faster, so the window is narrower rather than absent. A vendor branch would mean the safe path
is the one exercised least, and the correctness property (never conclude non-existence from one
unindexed search) is not vendor-specific. The cost on Cloud is a create deferred by at most one pass
in a rare crash-recovery path.

**Rejected: leaving the binding pending forever on repeated misses.** It is safer against duplicates
but a genuinely-never-created ticket would then never sync at all — trading a rare duplicate for a
permanent silent omission. The corroboration rule bounds the wait instead.

**Rejected: a non-indexed confirmation for the keyless branch.** There is none — JQL is the only way to
find an issue by label, and the keyless state is by definition the one with no key to GET. That is why
the keyed branch is already correct and this one cannot use the same trick.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — the keyless-branch miss counter, the
  corroborated-unbind rule, an accessor exposing "keyless-pending and within the grace window", and the
  resolved-count correction.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` — `create_one` consults that accessor and
  defers the create while the binding is keyless-pending inside the grace window. (NOT `outbound_differ.py`:
  it is at the locked 800-LOC cap, and the write site is the better guard anyway.)
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests (new module).

## Testing

The oracle is a client that models the actual failure: the issue EXISTS but the search does not see it.

* **the whole path, which is the only test that proves the fix** — a lagging-index client where
  `create_issue` succeeds but `search_issues` returns empty. Drive crash -> recover -> differ -> create
  and assert EXACTLY ONE issue is created. A test asserting only "recover_pending did not unbind"
  passes today's code path while the duplicate is still written, which is the trap this closes.
* **the create is deferred, not dropped** — once the index catches up (search starts returning the
  issue), the next pass BINDS to the existing issue and still creates nothing.
* **corroborated unbind still works** — a genuinely-never-created ticket, after 3 misses AND past the
  grace window, unbinds and is then re-created, so the fix does not strand work forever.
* **the keyed branch is untouched** — its no-search determinism is asserted unchanged.
* **`recover_pending`'s return value** counts an entry left pending as NOT resolved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] under a lagging-index client (create succeeds, search returns empty), the full
      crash -> recover -> differ -> create path creates EXACTLY ONE issue, asserted by a test that
      FAILS against the current code
- [ ] the create gate consults keyless-pendingness, not only `get_jira_key(...) is None` — verified by
      reading `dispatch_one.create_one`; a fix confined to `recover_pending` does NOT satisfy this
- [ ] a single negative search never unbinds: unbinding requires >= 3 consecutive misses AND an entry
      older than the grace period, both asserted
- [ ] once the index catches up, the pending binding CONFIRMS against the existing issue and no second
      issue is created, asserted
- [ ] a genuinely-absent issue still unbinds after corroboration and is re-created, so no ticket is
      stranded permanently pending
- [ ] the KEYED-pending branch still performs NO search, asserted, since it is already correct
- [ ] `recover_pending` does not count a still-pending entry as resolved
- [ ] the Cloud path is asserted unaffected in behaviour beyond the deferral, since this changes shared
      code
- [ ] the reason (DC Lucene eventual consistency) is documented at both call sites so the next reader
      does not "simplify" the grace window away

gate the create on keyless-pendingness within the grace window
